input.title: Tolerance
input.premise: Ivo Lann wrote the model that decides how much water every clinic and district receives, and a courier's figures say the water arrives short. He cannot go to a Sump Row counter himself without becoming a story, so he asks the player, hypothetically, to go and look.

input.persona: Pleasant, hurried, always half somewhere else; asks hypothetically and means it literally. Wants a quarter that closes clean; fears a story with his model's name on it; would never falsify a figure, and would never check one he was not asked to.

input.title: The Check
input.summary: Ivo sends someone to look at the counter he will not visit. Once it is over, his model is cleared and he is not.

input.title: The Model Is Correct
input.epilogue: You watch the stamped measure go out short at the Weir Exchange counter. Ivo gets his answer: the model is correct. He finds he does not feel any cleaner for it, and closes the quarter anyway.

narrative.description: In the lobby where he works, Ivo Lann stops you with a coffee he forgot to drink and a courier's figures still open on his slate.
narrative.playerHint: Talk to Ivo Lann at work.
narrative.stake: He needs to know that he does not need to know; a man from the tower at a Sump Row counter is a story.

dialogue.opening: Hypothetically. If someone wanted to know whether a model was wrong or a counter was, they would look at the counter. I can't. I'd be a story.

choices.text: Are you sure the model is right?
choices.reply: The model is correct. What happens to the water after it leaves the model is a logistics question. I'd like it to stay one.

choices.text: I'll go and look at the Weir Exchange counter for you.
choices.reply: Thank you. Don't tell me what you see unless it's that I was right. Hypothetically.

narrative.description: At the Weir Exchange counter in Sump Row you watch a clerk stamp a full measure onto a canister that is not full.
narrative.playerHint: Go to the Weir Exchange counter.
narrative.stake: If nobody looks, Ivo's model carries the blame for a clerk, and his name ends up in a report he never wanted to be in.
